EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows no carbonyl-type band around 1700–1750 cm⁻¹, so candidates containing C=O groups (4–10, 3, 6) are unlikely.  
The strongest line at 1661 cm⁻¹ fits the C=C stretching region of conjugated alkenes (rule GFQ-010).  
Bands at 1455 and 1382 cm⁻¹ correspond to CH₃/CH₂ deformations (GFQ-003), typical of alkyl-substituted hydrocarbons.  
Mid-frequency bands 1227 and 1157 cm⁻¹ match =C–H in-plane bends and C–C stretches seen in dienes, while the doublet 864/839 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of out-of-plane =C–H wags of substituted alkenes.  
The only high-wavenumber feature is the C–H stretch at 2913 cm⁻¹, consistent with an sp³-rich hydrocarbon; no >3000 cm⁻¹ =C–H stretch is prominent, as expected for a highly substituted diene.  
Among the candidates, CC(C)=CC=C(C)C (candidate 1) is the only purely hydrocarbon conjugated diene bearing several methyl groups, providing all the required CH₃ vibrations without introducing absent functional-group bands.
